Home.aboutTitle: I design and build digital products that are clear, useful, and ready to ship.
Home.aboutIntro: Hi, I’m Yeganeh Heshmat, a Product Designer and Front-End Developer with more than five years of experience taking ideas from rough concept to real, working products. I like working where business goals, design, and code meet. Usually that means getting involved early to shape the product direction, talking to users to understand what they actually need, and then designing the experience and building the interface myself. I care about how a product looks, but I care more about whether it makes sense for the people using it, supports the business, and can really be built and shipped.

techArchitecture.heading: Frontend Architecture
techArchitecture.mobileDescription: Tools for a fast, seamless experience

scalability.title: Scalability
scalability.body: I chose Next.js for TealNex because its scalable architecture supports the gradual expansion of the website. New sections, including architectural services, project portfolios, and interactive features, can be introduced without requiring significant changes to the underlying application structure.

routing.title: Structured Routing
routing.body: Next.js provides a file-based routing system that simplifies the organization of different website sections. This approach helps maintain a clear and manageable structure across service pages, architectural projects, renovation portfolios, and other content.

performance.title: Performance Optimization
performance.body: Next.js supports server-side rendering and static page generation, providing flexible strategies for delivering website content efficiently. These capabilities are particularly valuable for TealNex, where architectural photography and visual presentations play an essential role in the user experience.

seo.title: Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
seo.body: Next.js offers flexible rendering strategies and metadata management capabilities that support search engine optimization. This provides a strong technical foundation for improving the discoverability of architectural services, completed projects, and other website content.

ecosystem.title: Ecosystem & Maintainability
ecosystem.body: The extensive React and Next.js ecosystems, active developer communities, and comprehensive documentation simplify long-term maintenance. These advantages also facilitate troubleshooting, implementing new features, and keeping the website aligned with evolving technical requirements.

responsive.title: Responsive Design
responsive.body: I used Tailwind CSS to develop a responsive interface for TealNex, ensuring that architectural galleries, service pages, and contact forms adapt effectively to different screen sizes. This approach helps deliver a consistent browsing experience across mobile devices, tablets, and desktop computers.

consistency.title: Design Consistency
consistency.body: Tailwind CSS provides a structured styling system for maintaining consistent colors, spacing, typography, and visual properties throughout the website. This consistency helps preserve TealNex's visual identity while establishing a cohesive appearance across different pages and interface components.

efficiency.title: Development Efficiency
efficiency.body: Tailwind CSS follows a utility-first approach that accelerates interface development by reducing the need for extensive custom CSS. This makes it easier to implement layouts, refine visual details, and introduce design adjustments throughout the development process.

maintainability.title: Flexibility & Maintainability
maintainability.body: Tailwind CSS supports the development of reusable components and flexible interface layouts. This approach simplifies the gradual expansion of the website while keeping design patterns consistent and reducing the complexity of long-term styling maintenance.

optimization.title: CSS Optimization
optimization.body: Tailwind CSS generates styles based on the utility classes used throughout the project, helping minimize unnecessary CSS in production builds. This contributes to maintaining efficient stylesheet delivery, which is particularly valuable for a visually rich architectural website like TealNex.

interactive.title: Interactive State Management
interactive.body: I used Zustand to manage shared states across TealNex's interactive components. It enables efficient management of features such as project filtering, consultation request form steps, and temporary interface states. This approach helps maintain organized, predictable, and consistent interactions between different components throughout the website.

architecture.title: Lightweight & Modular Architecture
architecture.body: Zustand's lightweight and straightforward architecture allows application states to be organized into independent, reusable stores. This approach reduces dependencies between components, prevents unnecessary complexity, and helps maintain a clean and well-structured codebase across different sections of TealNex.

updates.title: Efficient Component Updates
updates.body: Zustand supports selective state subscriptions, allowing React components to update only when their relevant data changes. This capability helps minimize unnecessary re-renders and maintain smooth interface performance, particularly in dynamic and interactive sections of the website.

maintenance.title: Debugging & Maintainability
maintenance.body: Centralizing shared application states through Zustand makes data flow between components more transparent and manageable. This structure simplifies debugging, testing interactive behaviors, and maintaining the codebase while reducing the risk of unexpected issues when implementing changes across different website features.

scalability.title: Scalability & Flexibility
scalability.body: Zustand's flexible architecture supports the gradual expansion of TealNex's interactive functionality. As new features are introduced, such as advanced project filtering, multi-step forms, and interactive 3D visualization controls, additional state management requirements can be integrated without requiring significant modifications to the existing front-end architecture.

visualization.title: 3D Visualization
visualization.body: I integrated Three.js into TealNex to develop an interactive feature intended to present user-uploaded 2D images as a simplified three-dimensional representation of an interior space. The objective is to help users better understand the spatial characteristics of a room before beginning an architectural or renovation project.

rendering.title: Web-Based 3D Rendering
rendering.body: Three.js enables three-dimensional scenes to be rendered directly in the browser through WebGL. This approach allows users to explore initial room visualizations without installing specialized architectural modeling software or relying on external applications.

exploration.title: Interactive Exploration
exploration.body: Three.js provides camera controls, rotation, and zoom capabilities that enable users to examine a virtual environment from different perspectives. These interactions offer a more immersive way to evaluate interior spaces compared with conventional static images.

materials.title: Materials & Textures
materials.body: The library provides tools for managing surface materials, lighting, and image-based textures within 3D scenes. These capabilities are particularly useful for representing walls, flooring, and other interior elements while creating a more detailed visual interpretation of architectural spaces.

extensibility.title: Flexibility & Extensibility
extensibility.body: The flexible architecture of Three.js supports the gradual development of TealNex's 3D visualization feature. Starting with simplified room representations, the functionality can evolve to include more detailed geometry, improved rendering quality, and advanced interactive capabilities.

catalog.title: Digital Catalog
catalog.body: I used PDF.js to develop a digital architectural catalog for TealNex, designed to organize and present architectural concepts, floor plans, and design inspirations in a compact and accessible format. The goal is to provide users with a convenient way to explore design references directly through the website.

viewing.title: In-Browser Viewing
viewing.body: PDF.js enables PDF documents to be rendered directly within web browsers, eliminating the need for users to download files or install additional software. This creates a more seamless browsing experience while keeping architectural catalogs integrated into the website.

navigation.title: Page Navigation & Zoom
navigation.body: PDF.js provides the foundation for implementing page navigation and zoom controls, allowing users to move between catalog pages and examine architectural drawings in greater detail. These capabilities are particularly valuable when reviewing floor plans, layouts, and complex design elements.

preview.title: Visual Preview
preview.body: The library supports rendering PDF pages at different resolutions, enabling the creation of page thumbnails and visual previews. This functionality helps users navigate architectural catalogs more efficiently and identify relevant designs without opening each page individually.

integration.title: Integration & Extensibility
integration.body: The flexibility of PDF.js allows the development of a customized document viewer that aligns with TealNex's visual identity. Its extensible architecture also supports future improvements, including enhanced navigation, additional interactive controls, and more sophisticated catalog browsing experiences.

techArchitecture.heading: Frontend Architecture
techArchitecture.mobileDescription: Tools for fast, seamless tile shopping

dexie.description: Stores and manages local data to preserve shopping cart information and user selections across sessions

storage.title: Local Data Storage
storage.body: I used Dexie.js to manage persistent client-side data within TileTail's front-end architecture. By providing a simplified interface for IndexedDB, Dexie.js enables the browser to store information such as recently viewed products, temporary user selections, and data associated with the purchasing process. This approach helps preserve useful information locally while reducing the need for repeated network requests during certain interactions.

persistence.title: Shopping Data Persistence
persistence.body: Dexie.js provides a reliable foundation for storing temporary shopping information, including selected tile products, quantities, and certain order preferences. When integrated with Zustand, it can help preserve relevant shopping cart information across page reloads and returning visits. In this architecture, Zustand manages active application state, while Dexie.js handles persistent browser storage, allowing the shopping experience to remain more consistent across sessions.

offline.title: Fast Access & Offline Support
offline.body: Using IndexedDB through Dexie.js allows previously stored data to be retrieved directly from the browser without requiring additional server requests. This capability improves access to locally available product information and previous user selections while supporting limited functionality during temporary network interruptions. However, current pricing, product availability, and affiliate information still require synchronization with their respective servers or external APIs.

structured.title: Structured Data Management
structured.body: Dexie.js provides structured database management through tables, indexes, and query capabilities built on IndexedDB. These features help organize locally stored product information, tile attributes, and temporary order data. Separating storage logic from interface components also makes the codebase easier to maintain and provides a more predictable approach to managing browser-side information across different shopping features.

integration.title: Integration & Extensibility
integration.body: Dexie.js can operate alongside Zustand and TanStack Query as part of TileTail's front-end architecture. Zustand manages interactive application states, TanStack Query handles server data fetching and API caching, and Dexie.js provides persistent local storage. This separation of responsibilities supports future functionality such as saving unfinished orders, preserving user preferences, and restoring locally stored information when customers return to the website.

zod.description: Validates form inputs and service request data with consistent rules.

purchase.title: Purchase Form Validation
purchase.body: I used Zod to validate user input across TileTail's purchasing and checkout forms. The library enables the definition of structured validation rules for required fields, data types, and input formats. By checking submitted information against these rules, the application can identify incomplete or invalid entries before processing a purchase request. This approach helps reduce input errors and creates a more reliable and organized checkout experience.

installers.title: Installer Form Validation
installers.body: In addition to selling tiles, TileTail provides installation-related services that require collecting and managing information from installers. I used Zod to validate data entered into installer registration and information forms, including personal details, contact information, and other required fields. Consistent validation rules help ensure that installer information follows the expected structure while reducing the likelihood of incomplete or incorrectly formatted submissions.

profile.title: Address & Profile Validation
profile.body: I used Zod to manage validation across address registration, contact information, and user profile forms. The library allows required fields, input formats, and other constraints to be defined consistently throughout the application. Accurate validation is particularly important when customers provide delivery addresses for tile orders or location information for installation services. This approach helps maintain more consistent user information across different sections of the platform.

schemas.title: Schema-Based Validation & Type Safety
schemas.body: Zod provides a schema-based approach that allows validation rules to be defined centrally and reused across multiple forms and components. Its integration with TypeScript also enables types to be inferred directly from validation schemas, reducing inconsistencies between data structures and validation requirements. For TileTail, which contains numerous forms related to purchasing, installation services, and account management, this architecture helps maintain a cleaner, more predictable, and easier-to-maintain codebase.

errors.title: Error Handling & User Experience
errors.body: Zod enables structured validation errors that can be used to provide clear feedback when users enter incorrect or incomplete information. This allows customers and installers to identify and correct mistakes before submitting forms. By improving the clarity of validation messages and reducing unsuccessful submissions, the application creates a smoother and more predictable experience. Centralized validation schemas also simplify future updates to form requirements and reduce the complexity of maintaining validation logic across the website.

pdfjs.description: Displays PDF documents directly within the website.

invoices.title: Purchase Invoice Viewing
invoices.body: I used PDF.js to develop the front-end document viewing functionality for TileTail's purchase invoices. After a customer completes an order, the backend generates the corresponding invoice as a PDF document. PDF.js allows this document to be rendered directly within the website, enabling users to review purchased products, order details, and invoice amounts without installing additional software or relying on external PDF viewing applications.

integration.title: Invoice System Integration
integration.body: TileTail separates invoice generation from document presentation, with the backend responsible for creating and issuing invoices and PDF.js handling their rendering within the front-end interface. This separation allows both systems to evolve independently while maintaining a consistent user experience. Customers can access their generated invoices through the relevant order sections, creating a seamless connection between purchasing, order management, and financial document viewing.

catalog.title: Product Catalog Viewing
catalog.body: I used PDF.js to display digital catalogs associated with tile and ceramic products. Some products include PDF catalogs containing visual references, technical specifications, dimensions, color variations, and additional product information. Rendering these documents directly within TileTail allows customers to explore product details before making purchasing decisions. This functionality is particularly useful for tile collections that require closer examination of materials, finishes, and technical characteristics.

affiliate.title: Affiliate Catalog Integration
affiliate.body: Since TileTail supports an Affiliate Marketing model, part of its product information is retrieved from external suppliers and retail partners through APIs. When these providers supply PDF catalogs or catalog URLs, PDF.js enables the documents to be presented within TileTail's interface. This integration allows customers to review additional information about externally listed products before being redirected to the supplier's website, creating a more informative and consistent product discovery experience.

viewing.title: Interactive Viewing & User Experience
viewing.body: PDF.js provides the foundation for rendering PDF pages, navigating multi-page documents, and implementing interactive controls such as zooming and page selection. These capabilities support the development of a customized document viewer aligned with TileTail's visual identity. The same viewing infrastructure can serve both purchase invoices and product catalogs while supporting future improvements such as page thumbnails, enhanced navigation controls, and more convenient document exploration.

tanstack.description: Manages fetching and caching for product listings, filters, and store information.

products.title: Product Data Fetching & Management
products.body: I used TanStack Query to manage product information retrieved from multiple APIs within TileTail's shopping platform. In addition to selling its own products, TileTail supports an Affiliate Marketing model that allows products from external retailers and suppliers to be displayed alongside its internal catalog. TanStack Query provides a structured approach to requesting, retrieving, and managing this external product data, simplifying the integration of multiple data sources into the website.

caching.title: Caching & Request Optimization
caching.body: TanStack Query provides caching mechanisms that temporarily store product information retrieved from external retailer APIs. This reduces redundant network requests when users navigate between product categories, revisit previously viewed sections, or return to product listings. By reusing cached data when appropriate, the application can improve browsing performance, reduce unnecessary API traffic, and provide faster access to product information across TileTail's catalog.

synchronization.title: Data Synchronization & Background Refetching
synchronization.body: TanStack Query supports configurable data freshness policies and background refetching, helping the application maintain more up-to-date information from affiliate partners. This is particularly important because external product details, including prices, availability, and specifications, may change over time. By defining appropriate synchronization and refetching strategies, TileTail can keep displayed product information better aligned with external sources while reducing the need for manual page refreshes.

states.title: Loading States & Error Handling
states.body: TanStack Query provides structured mechanisms for managing loading, success, and error states associated with API requests. These features make it possible to display appropriate loading indicators, handle unavailable data, and implement retry strategies when external services experience temporary failures. Since TileTail retrieves affiliate product information from multiple independent providers, reliable request-state management helps maintain a consistent browsing experience even when individual APIs encounter connectivity or availability issues.

affiliate.title: Affiliate Marketing Integration
affiliate.body: I used TanStack Query to manage product information received from affiliate partners and integrate it into TileTail's product browsing experience. Users can explore product images and essential details from external retailers alongside TileTail's own inventory. When an affiliate product is selected, the website's navigation logic redirects users to the corresponding product page on the supplier's website, while TileTail's own products follow the internal purchasing process. This architecture expands the available product selection without requiring the business to maintain inventory for every listed item.

tailwind.description: Creates consistent styling and responsive layouts across mobile and desktop.

responsive.title: Responsive Design
responsive.body: I used Tailwind CSS to develop TileTail's responsive user interface, ensuring that product listings, tile categories, shopping cart components, checkout forms, and installation service pages adapt effectively to different screen sizes. This approach allows product grids, images, navigation elements, and interactive components to adjust across mobile devices, tablets, and desktop computers. The result is a more consistent and accessible shopping experience across different devices.

consistency.title: Design Consistency
consistency.body: Tailwind CSS provides a structured styling system for maintaining consistent colors, spacing, typography, sizing, and visual patterns throughout TileTail. Shared interface elements, including product cards, purchase buttons, forms, shopping cart components, and service sections, follow a cohesive design language. This consistency helps preserve the platform's visual identity while providing users with familiar and predictable interactions as they navigate between different shopping and service experiences.

efficiency.title: Development Efficiency
efficiency.body: Tailwind CSS follows a utility-first approach that accelerates interface development by reducing the need for extensive custom CSS. This is particularly valuable when building TileTail's diverse sections, including product catalogs, tile detail pages, checkout forms, user profiles, and installation service interfaces. Utility classes make it easier to implement layouts, refine spacing, adjust visual elements, and introduce design changes efficiently throughout the development process.

maintainability.title: Flexibility & Maintainability
maintainability.body: Tailwind CSS supports reusable components and flexible interface layouts while helping maintain consistent styling patterns across the application. This approach is particularly useful for TileTail, where both internally sold products and affiliate products can share common presentation components. It also simplifies the development of additional product categories, new service pages, and evolving shopping features without introducing unnecessary styling complexity or compromising visual consistency.

optimization.title: CSS Optimization
optimization.body: Tailwind CSS generates styles based on the utility classes used throughout the project, helping minimize unnecessary CSS in production builds. This contributes to more efficient stylesheet delivery and better control over front-end asset sizes. For TileTail, a visually rich e-commerce platform featuring extensive tile photography, product catalogs, and interactive shopping components, optimized styling complements other performance improvements and supports a smoother browsing experience

scalability.title: Scalability
scalability.body: I used Next.js to develop TileTail's front-end architecture, establishing a flexible and scalable foundation for the platform's tile sales, installation services, and design-related features. This architecture supports the gradual expansion of product catalogs, service pages, and interactive functionality without requiring significant modifications to the website's underlying structure.

routing.title: Structured Routing
routing.body: Next.js provides a file-based routing system that simplifies the organization and management of different website sections. This approach allows product listings, tile categories, installation services, design collections, and company information to be structured independently. It also supports clear navigation paths, helping users move efficiently between products and services while maintaining an organized and maintainable application structure.

performance.title: Performance Optimization
performance.body: Next.js supports multiple rendering strategies, including Server-Side Rendering and Static Site Generation, providing flexibility in how website content is delivered. These capabilities are particularly valuable for TileTail, where product photography, tile textures, and interior design examples play an essential role in the browsing experience. Appropriate rendering strategies can improve content delivery, reduce loading times, and provide smoother navigation across product and service pages.

seo.title: Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
seo.body: Next.js offers rendering capabilities and metadata management features that establish a strong technical foundation for search engine optimization. These features support the discoverability and indexing of tile products, product categories, installation services, and design-related content. By organizing pages and metadata effectively, the website can improve its visibility in search results and make relevant products and services more accessible to potential customers.

ecosystem.title: Ecosystem & Maintainability
ecosystem.body: The extensive React and Next.js ecosystems, comprehensive documentation, and active developer communities simplify long-term development and maintenance. The component-based architecture promotes reusable interface elements across product listings, service pages, and interactive features. This approach helps maintain consistent implementation patterns while making it easier to troubleshoot issues, introduce new functionality, and adapt the platform to evolving business requirements.

cart.title: Shopping Cart State Management
cart.body: I used Zustand to manage shared application states across TileTail's shopping cart functionality. This includes handling selected products, product quantities, and changes to shopping cart contents. Users can add tiles to their cart, adjust quantities, or remove items while immediately seeing the results of their actions. Zustand's lightweight architecture helps maintain predictable and responsive interactions throughout the purchasing experience.

centralized.title: Centralized State Management
centralized.body: Zustand allows shared shopping cart information to be organized into independent, reusable stores. This approach helps synchronize data across product cards, product detail pages, shopping cart indicators, and order review sections. By maintaining shared state in a centralized structure, the application reduces unnecessary data passing between components and helps ensure consistent cart information throughout different sections of the store.

realtime.title: Real-Time State Updates
realtime.body: Zustand enables immediate updates to application state, allowing relevant interface components to reflect changes without requiring a full page reload. When users add products, modify quantities, or remove items, displayed information such as cart item counts and calculated totals can update automatically. This capability creates a more interactive shopping experience and provides users with immediate feedback during the purchasing process.

updates.title: Efficient Component Updates
updates.body: Zustand supports selective state subscriptions, allowing React components to update only when the data they depend on changes. This reduces unnecessary re-renders and helps maintain smooth interface performance across product listings, shopping cart components, and other interactive elements. Such optimization is particularly valuable for TileTail, where visually rich product catalogs and frequent shopping cart interactions are essential parts of the user experience.

scalability.title: Scalability & Maintainability
scalability.body: Zustand's lightweight and modular architecture supports the gradual expansion of TileTail's shopping functionality. Additional requirements, such as managing product variations, advanced filtering, multi-step checkout processes, and other interactive shopping features, can be introduced without significantly restructuring the existing front-end application. Centralized state management also simplifies debugging, testing, and maintaining application behavior over time.
